module: 3.5 Cancer Health Disparities and Social Determinants
claim: Researchers have found that TNBC is more prevalent in Black women who trace their ancestry to West Africa, and more specifically to Ghana.

evidence.quote: TNBC frequency was higher for AA and Gh patients (41% and 54%, respectively) compared with WA and Eth patients (23% and 15%, respectively; P < .001)
evidence.note: TNBC frequency 54% in Ghanaian/West African patients, higher than white American and Ethiopian patients. Strict re-read: the quote does not state West African/Ghanaian ancestry and 'Black women' not explicit; only frequency comparison of coded groups.

evidence.quote: Pooled TNBC frequency was highest across West Africa, 45.7% (n=15, 95% CI: 38.8% to 52.8%, I2=91%) and lowest in Central Africa, 14.9% (n=1, 95% CI: 8.9 % to 24.1%).
evidence.note: TNBC frequency highest in West Africa (45.7%) among indigenous African women; not about ancestry of Black women elsewhere.

module: 3.5 Cancer Health Disparities and Social Determinants
claim: The model is based on the premise that social setting contributes to disease outcome and considers 3 major variables, ie, poverty, culture, and social justice, and posits an important connection between the social determinants of health and health inequities.

evidence.quote: The lenses--Social Justice, Culture-Place, and Organizational Capacity-Organizing Approach--assist health professional-community partnerships in planning and evaluating community organizing-based health promotion programs.
evidence.note: Three lenses include social justice and culture, but third is organizational capacity, not poverty; childhood obesity context.

claim: An indicator of mitotic activity, the Ki-67 labeling index, is usually below 10% for low-grade gliomas.

evidence.quote: Of the tumor specimens, 29% had a negative Ki-67 index (i.e., zero Ki-67 positive cells) and 7.7% had an average Ki-67 index of >/=5%.
evidence.note: In 180 low-grade gliomas, only 7.7% averaged 5% or more, implying most were below 10%. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Low-grade gliomas and Ki-67 usually below 10% not stated.

evidence.quote: Lower indices were found in meningiomas (median: 1.84) and the lowest were seen in low-grade gliomas (grades 1, 2) (median: 0.85), dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumors (median: 0.63), and gangliogliomas (median: 0.50).
evidence.note: Pediatric low-grade gliomas had median Ki-67 LI 0.85; a median, not a statement that it is usually below 10%.

claim: Primary CNS tumors comprise approximately 50% to 70% of intracranial tumors, with the majority being neuroepithelial tissue tumors.

evidence.quote: The most frequent intracranial tumors were those of neuroepithelial tissue, accounting for 58.3% of all CNS neoplasms (annual incidence, 6.9/100000 population).
evidence.note: Neuroepithelial tumors most frequent (58.3% of CNS neoplasms) in one Croatian area; no primary-tumor share of intracranial tumors.

evidence.quote: RESULTS: Out of 175 subjects, 95 had primary CNS tumors and 80 had metastases.
evidence.note: Gives 95 primary CNS tumors vs 80 metastases in one cohort; no percentage of intracranial tumors stated.

claim: MammaPrint is the first assay based on microarrays that has completed the path from the bench to FDA approval for clinical application.

evidence.note: Earliest MammaPrint entry: decision date 2007-06-22; record shows 510(k) clearance, no "first" or "approval" statement.

evidence.quote: Substantially Equivalent
evidence.note: Decision was Substantially Equivalent via Traditional 510(k), i.e. clearance rather than approval.

claim: A 50-gene molecular signature (PAM50) was developed for clinical use in prognosis and treatment decisions, enabling molecular subtype classification from gene expression data.

evidence.quote: PAM50 subtypes, which are based on gene-expression patterns10,11
evidence.note: Says PAM50 subtypes derive from gene-expression patterns; gives no gene count or intended clinical uses.

evidence.quote: In this prespecified correlative analysis of the GEICAM/CIBOMA trial, PAM50 non-basal status identified patients with early-stage TNBC most likely to benefit from capecitabine.
evidence.note: PAM50 subtype used to predict treatment benefit; supports treatment-decision use, not the 50-gene count.

claim: Gene expression profiling revolutionized breast cancer classification in the early 2000s, revealing that breast cancer comprises several distinct biologic entities that are only partially captured by immunohistochemical markers.

evidence.quote: Under ASCO/CAP guidelines, tumors with 1-10% ER staining would be classified as ER positive, yet most are basal like or HER2 enriched and have pathological features similar to ER-negative tumors.
evidence.note: Shows IHC ER classification only partly matches molecular subtype; no statement on early-2000s expression profiling.

claim: Most breast cancer is sporadic (90%-95%), with only 5% to 10% of patients having an identifiable genetic mutation.

evidence.quote: The ability to distinguish a growing proportion of the 5% to 10% of all cancers that develop in individuals who have inherited a genetic mutation conferring heightened susceptibility to specific cancers may permit targeted efforts in cancer surveillance and prevention.
evidence.note: Gives 5-10% hereditary for all cancers, not breast cancer specifically.

claim: Approximately 80% of lung cancer cases in men and 90% of cases in women are associated with smoking.

evidence.quote: The AF of lung cancer linked to smoking was about 87%, and around 3049 cases of this cancer in men could be avoided if tobacco use could be prevented.
evidence.note: Morocco estimate of about 87% lung cancer attributable to smoking; not split 80% men and 90% women.

claim: NSCLC is now recognized not as a singular entity but as multiple pathologies with unique molecular signatures.

evidence.quote: Molecular diagnostics now play a pivotal role in guiding treatment strategies, with actionable genomic alterations (AGAs) informing the use of EGFR, ALK, ROS1, KRAS, NRG1, and other targeted inhibitors in both early and advanced settings.
evidence.note: Lists molecular alterations (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, KRAS, NRG1) defining NSCLC treatment groups; does not call NSCLC multiple entities.

evidence.quote: Lung cancer is a highly heterogeneous disease.
evidence.note: States lung cancer heterogeneity generally; no named molecular subtypes of NSCLC.

claim: Due to different triggering mutations and critical mutations in the GBM stem cells, GBM is classified into primary tumors arising from neural stem cell precursors and secondary tumors arising from mutations in mature neural cells like astrocytes.

evidence.quote: The presence of different triggering mutations on the background of the presence of key mutations in the GBM stem cells (GBMsc) further separates GBM as primary arising de novo from neural stem cell precursors developing into GBMsc and secondary, by means of aggregated mutations.
evidence.note: Primary GBM from neural stem cell precursors matches; secondary is by aggregated mutations, no mature cell or astrocyte origin stated.

claim: GBM is usually associated with pseudoprogression or radionecrosis, which is a subacute worsening of MRI findings that occur within 3 months after the completion of chemoradiotherapy.

evidence.quote: Although typically occurring during the first 3 months after radiochemotherapy, PsP may occur later in the course of the disease and may then be particularly difficult to distinguish from true tumor progression.
evidence.note: Pseudoprogression typically occurs within the first 3 months after radiochemotherapy in glioblastoma, though it can occur later. Strict re-read: the quote does not state GBM association, radionecrosis, MRI worsening definition not stated; only PsP timing.

claim: Results from some epidemiological studies suggest that ionizing radiation can increase the chance of developing gliomas.

evidence.quote: Most significantly, these include an increase in risk by exposure to ionizing radiation and a decrease in risk by history of allergies or atopic disease(s).
evidence.note: Review states ionizing radiation exposure increases glioma risk. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Gliomas not named in quote; not stated as epidemiological studies of glioma.

evidence.quote: The increased risk of RIGs is well described in both the pediatric and adult populations and after the use of both therapeutic and diagnostic radiations.
evidence.note: States increased risk of radiation-induced gliomas after radiation exposure. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Gliomas not named (only abbreviation RIGs); epidemiological studies not mentioned.

claim: The landmark 2005 EORTC-NCIC trial established the current gold standard for newly diagnosed glioblastoma treatment, known as the Stupp protocol.

evidence.quote: Adult patients with newly diagnosed glioblastoma were randomly assigned to receive either standard radiotherapy or identical radiotherapy with concomitant temozolomide followed by up to six cycles of adjuvant temozolomide.
evidence.note: Gives the EORTC-NCIC trial arms; record dates the original report 2004 and does not use the name Stupp.

evidence.quote: Standard treatment for patients with newly diagnosed glioblastoma includes surgery, radiotherapy (RT), and temozolomide (TMZ) chemotherapy (TMZ/RT→TMZ).
evidence.note: States temozolomide plus radiotherapy is standard treatment for newly diagnosed glioblastoma; does not credit the trial. Strict re-read: the quote does not state 2005 EORTC-NCIC trial establishing standard and the Stupp protocol not stated.

claim: The only well-established causative factor is exposure to high doses of ionizing radiation.

evidence.quote: The reported risk factors for glioblastoma (GBM), i.e., ionizing radiation, Li-Fraumeni syndrome, Neurofibromatosis I, and Turcot syndrome, also increase the risk of other brain tumor types.
evidence.note: Lists ionizing radiation plus genetic syndromes as reported GBM risk factors, so radiation is not the only one named.

claim: The risk of surgical site infection increases with irradiation and multiple surgeries.

evidence.quote: Three or more surgeries were an independent factor triggering SSIs (P = 0.02); in contrast, radiation therapy was not an independent factor for SSIs (P = 0.07).
evidence.note: Glioma cohort: repeat surgeries independently raise SSI risk; radiation was associated only in univariate analysis, not independent.

claim: The rate of recurrence and the risk of transformation to malignancy is dependent on the histopathological type of meningioma.

evidence.quote: High-grade meningiomas (atypical and anaplastic/malignant) are at increased risk of recurrence following primary treatment with maximum safe surgical resection.
evidence.note: Recurrence risk is higher in high-grade meningiomas; malignant transformation risk by type is not stated.

claim: The recurrence and mortality are lower for intraventricular meningiomas than in other localizations.

evidence.quote: Their recurrence rate is lower than that of extra-axial meningiomas, but their surgical resection can be burdened with life-threatening complications, which represent the major cause of the reported 4% mortality.
evidence.note: Recurrence lower than extra-axial meningiomas matches; mortality (4%) is given without comparison to other locations.

claim: Various genetic susceptibility loci have been identified for gliomas, and two distinct susceptibility loci have been associated with meningiomas.

evidence.quote: We identified five new loci for glioblastoma (GBM) at 1p31.3 (rs12752552; P = 2.04 × 10-9, odds ratio (OR) = 1.22)
evidence.note: one instance: GWAS meta-analysis finds new glioma susceptibility loci (five GBM, eight non-GBM); no meningioma loci stated.

claim: CML typically arises from reciprocal translocation and fusion of BCR on chromosome 22 and ABL1 on chromosome 9, resulting in dysregulated tyrosine kinase on chromosome 22 called the Philadelphia (Ph) chromosome.

evidence.quote: A reciprocal translocation between chromosomes 22 and 9 produces the Philadelphia chromosome, which is often found in patients with chronic myelogenous leukemia. The chromosome 22 breakpoint for this translocation is located within the BCR gene.
evidence.note: Reciprocal 22;9 translocation gives Philadelphia chromosome in CML, with BCR at the chromosome 22 breakpoint. Strict re-read: the quote does not state ABL1 fusion partner and dysregulated tyrosine kinase not stated.

claim: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors are effective in most cases; however, the patient's non-compliance is a prominent cause of failure.

evidence.quote: Non-adherence to therapy contributes greatly to treatment failure.
evidence.note: In CML, non-adherence is said to contribute greatly to therapy failure; TKI efficacy in most cases not quantified. Strict re-read: the quote does not state TKIs not named; 'effective in most cases' not stated.

claim: Adult T-cell lymphoma and mycosis fungoides are the most common mature T cell lymphomas.

evidence.quote: Mycosis fungoides (MF) is the commonest subtype of cutaneous lymphoma, characterized by the infiltration of malignant T-cell clones into the skin. It accounts for approximately 60% of all cutaneous T-cell lymphoma diagnoses.
evidence.note: MF is most common cutaneous (T-cell) lymphoma; nothing on adult T-cell lymphoma or all mature T-cell lymphomas.

claim: The disease is associated with Epstein Barr Virus (EBV), human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), and chromosomal translocations that cause the overexpression of oncogene C-MYC.

evidence.quote: It is characterized by a translocation involving the MYC oncogene. Three subtypes of Burkitt lymphoma are recognized: the endemic form, occurring primarily in Africa and associated with the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV); the sporadic form, representing less than 3 % of all non-Hodgkin lymphomas (NHL); and the immunodeficiency-associated form, occurring primarily in HIV-infected patients.
evidence.note: Links Burkitt lymphoma to MYC translocation, EBV (endemic form) and HIV (immunodeficiency form). Strict re-read: the quote does not state Overexpression of MYC caused by translocation not stated.

claim: Monoclonal protein (M-protein) exists in about 3% of adults older than 50 years and increases to 5% in those older than 70 years.

evidence.quote: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance is relatively common in the general population, with a prevalence of 3% to 4% among individuals older than age 50 years.
evidence.note: Gives 3% to 4% prevalence of MGUS over age 50; no higher figure for those over 70.

claim: SBP shows progression to PCM or multiple plasmacytoma in up to 70% of cases, therefore close observation and follow up is crucial.

evidence.quote: The 10-year multiple myeloma-free survival rates were: SPB, 30%; EMP, 90%; and overall, 50%.
evidence.note: Gives 10-year myeloma-free survival of 30% for solitary bone plasmacytoma, implying about 70% progression; progression percentage not stated directly.

claim: Solitary plasmacytoma is the most common form of plasmacytoma.

evidence.quote: SPB accounted for 55.2%, SEP for 44.4% and MSP for 3.4% of the cases.
evidence.note: Among 29 solitary plasmacytoma cases, bone and extramedullary forms dominate over multiple solitary; no comparison with non-solitary forms.

claim: The mildest and most common PCD is the precancerous monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS), affecting approximately 3 percent of the general population 50 years of age or older.

evidence.quote: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance is relatively common in the general population, with a prevalence of 3% to 4% among individuals older than age 50 years.
evidence.note: Gives MGUS prevalence of 3% to 4% in people over 50, consistent with about 3 percent. Strict re-read: the quote does not state 'Mildest and most common PCD' and precancerous status not stated.

claim: FDG PET/CT scan is considered to have superior sensitivity because of the FDG avidity in some T-cell lymphomas and helps in staging and treatment response assessment.

evidence.quote: The diagnostic sensitivity, specificity and accuracy of AITL using CT were 78.3%, 100%, and 87.8%, respectively; using PET/CT, these values were 98.9%, 100%, and 99.4%, respectively.
evidence.note: In angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma only, PET/CT sensitivity (98.9%) exceeded CT (78.3%); one subtype.

evidence.quote: PET/CT is very valuable in the diagnosis and staging of AITL.
evidence.note: Supports PET/CT usefulness in staging for one T-cell lymphoma subtype (AITL).

claim: Patients with multiple myeloma and other monoclonal gammopathies often have kidney dysfunction due to a wide range of associated pathologies.

evidence.quote: Symptomatic multiple myeloma is commonly complicated by acute kidney injury through various mechanisms.
evidence.note: States acute kidney injury commonly complicates symptomatic myeloma; other gammopathies and exact frequency not given. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Monoclonal gammopathies other than myeloma and 'wide range of pathologies' not stated.

claim: Cranial irradiation, a history of intrathecal chemotherapy, older age at the time of treatment, and hematopoietic cell transplantation can lead to neurologic and psychiatric complications like post-traumatic stress disorder.

evidence.quote: Survivors of the acute lymphocytic leukemia, central nervous system tumors, and stem cell transplant have frequently been exposed to cranial radiation, systemic and intrathecal chemotherapy, which places them at risk of developing chronic leukoencephalopathy.
evidence.note: Links cranial radiation and intrathecal chemotherapy to neurologic late effects; no mention of PTSD, age or transplant as cause.

evidence.quote: Certain treatment modalities, such as intrathecal methotrexate and radiation, have been shown to be associated with poor neurocognition; however, long-term outcomes remain highly variable.
evidence.note: Intrathecal methotrexate and radiation linked to neurocognitive late effects; no psychiatric outcome such as PTSD.

claim: MYCN Amplification : Present in approximately 20-25% of neuroblastomas, MYCN amplification is strongly associated with advanced-stage disease and poor prognosis.

evidence.quote: Amplification of the MYC family member, MYCN, is found in ∼25% of cases and correlates with high-risk disease and poor prognosis.
evidence.note: Gives about 25% MYCN amplification, linked to high-risk disease and poor prognosis; stage not stated explicitly. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Neuroblastoma named, 20-25% figure, and advanced-stage association not stated.

claim: Since neuroblastoma cells produce catecholamines, breakdown products including homovanillic acid (HVA) and vanillylmandelic acid (VMA) are elevated in urine in over 90% of cases.

evidence.quote: For 289 neuroblastoma patients at the time of diagnosis, the urinary excretion of VMA was significantly elevated in 75%, and HVA was elevated in 80%.
evidence.note: Gives proportions of neuroblastoma patients with elevated urinary VMA (75%) and HVA (80%) at diagnosis. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Quote gives 75% (VMA) and 80% (HVA), not over 90%.

claim: Genetic markers including WT1, CTNNB1, and WTX gene alterations are found in about one-third of all Wilms tumors, while poorer prognosis is linked to TP53 mutations and loss of heterozygosity at chromosomes 1p, 1q, 11p15, and 16q.

evidence.quote: This gene, which we call WTX, is inactivated in approximately one-third of Wilms tumors (15 of 51 tumors).
evidence.note: WTX alone is altered in about one-third; claim combines WT1, CTNNB1 and WTX.

evidence.quote: Somatic biallelic inactivation of WT1 is observed in 5-10% of sporadic WT. Somatic mutations in exon 3 of CTNNB1, which encodes β-catenin, were initially observed in 15% of WT.
evidence.note: Gives separate frequencies for WT1 (5-10%) and CTNNB1 (15%); no combined one-third figure.

claim: Includes male pseudo-hermaphroditism and progressive renal failure starting in infancy, with 90% of affected individuals eventually developing Wilms tumor.

evidence.quote: This rare syndrome is characterized by a rapid progressive nephropathy, male pseudohermaphroditism, and an increased risk for Wilms tumor.
evidence.note: Syndrome has increased Wilms tumor risk, but no 90% figure is given.

claim: Present-day survival rates are 80-90%, with the addition of radiation therapy significantly improving outcomes.

evidence.quote: Advances in multimodal therapy including surgery, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy given according to risk stratification have allowed most patients to achieve survival rates in excess of 90%.
evidence.note: Survival above 90% with multimodal therapy including radiation; no 80-90% range and no radiation-specific effect.

evidence.quote: Curative therapy is achievable in 90% of affected children, even those with disseminated disease, yet survival disparities within and between countries exist and deserve commitment to change.
evidence.note: Gives about 90% cure; does not state effect of adding radiation.

claim: The cause of Wilms tumor is believed to be due to genetic alterations affecting normal embryological development of the genitourinary tract.

evidence.quote: Wilms tumor (WT), an embryonic tumor arising from undifferentiated renal mesenchyme, has been a productive model for understanding the role of genes in both tumorigenesis and normal organogenesis.
evidence.note: Embryonic renal origin and genes in organogenesis; does not explicitly say genetic alterations cause it.

evidence.quote: Approximately 2% of WT patients have a family history of WT, and even sporadic WT is thought to have a strong genetic component to its etiology.
evidence.note: Genetic component to etiology, without mention of embryological development of the genitourinary tract.

claim: The median age of diagnosis is 3.5 years, with 90% of cases diagnosed before age 6.

evidence.quote: The median age-at-onset of Wilms tumor is 38 months in the U.S. National Wilms Tumor Study series, with cases in girls occurring on average 6 months later than in boys.
evidence.note: Median onset 38 months (about 3.2 years), not 3.5; no 90%-before-age-6 figure.

evidence.quote: The average of patients with bilateral tumours was 15 months, whereas that of patients with unilateral tumours was 31/2 years.
evidence.note: Average (not median) age 3.5 years for unilateral tumours in a small series; no 90% figure.

claim: There are notable racial differences, with higher incidence in Africans and African Americans, while East Asians have the lowest incidence and better survival outcomes.

evidence.quote: Wilms tumor (WT) is thought to arise in children of Black African ancestry with greater frequency than in Whites.
evidence.note: Supports higher incidence in Black African ancestry; says nothing on East Asians.

evidence.quote: Although overall survival from WT was not statistically different between Blacks (92.9%) and Whites (94.0%), Black males showed the lowest survival (85%; P = 0.21).
evidence.note: Tennessee survival by race; no East Asian survival data.

claim: Wilms tumor is thought to develop from persistent metanephric tissue or nephrogenic rests, which may occur in 1% of infantile kidneys but typically regress during childhood.

evidence.quote: Nephrogenic rests represent precursors of nephroblatoma and they are associated with certain syndromes carrying a high risk for nephroblastoma.
evidence.note: Rests are precursors of Wilms tumor; no 1% infant-kidney frequency given.

evidence.quote: The nephrogenic rests may undergo regression or proliferation with a high risk for development of a nephroblatoma.
evidence.note: Rests may regress or progress to tumor; frequency and 'typically regress' not stated.

claim: Deletions in 17p leading to loss of heterozygosity are also frequently reported.

evidence.quote: With 17p loss being the commonest chromosomal aberrance observed in our sample set, array-CGH were employed to first distinguish for 17p-positive cases.
evidence.note: 17p loss was the commonest aberration in this sample set; loss of heterozygosity not named. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Deletions leading to LOH; 'frequently reported' across literature, only 17p loss in own sample.

evidence.quote: Non-random allelic imbalances were identified on chromosomes 7q (58.3%), 8p (66.7%), 16q (58.3%), 17p (58.3%) and 17q (66.7%).
evidence.note: Allelic imbalance of 17p in 58.3% of 12 medulloblastomas; LOH not named specifically.

claim: Extraneural metastases occur in approximately 7% of pediatric cases, most commonly to bone (78%), lymph nodes (33%), liver (15%), and lungs (11%).

evidence.quote: Medulloblastoma is a malignant pediatric brain neoplasm with an unusual predilection for metastasis to the skeleton.
evidence.note: Supports bone as a metastatic site only; no 7% frequency or organ percentages.

claim: Medulloblastoma is thought to originate from granule cell precursors in the external germinal layer (EGL) of the developing cerebellum.

evidence.quote: Using RESTTG mice, we demonstrate that elevated REST expression in cerebellar granule cell progenitors, the cells of origin of sonic hedgehog (SHH) MBs, increased vascular growth.
evidence.note: Granule cell progenitors are origin of SHH medulloblastoma; external germinal layer not mentioned.

evidence.quote: We confirm that SHH and Group 3/4 medulloblastomas originate from the granule cell and unipolar brush cell lineages.
evidence.note: Granule cell lineage origin for SHH and Group 3/4; no external germinal layer stated.

claim: The highest survival rates are seen in WNT subgroup (97-100%), while Group 3 medulloblastoma has the worst outcomes (40-65%).

evidence.quote: Five-year overall survival differed by molecular subgroup (P = .006): WNT pathway activated, 100% (95% CI, 100%-100%); SHH pathway activated, 53.6% (95% CI, 33.0%-74.2%); group 3, 73.7% (95% CI, 61.9%-85.5%); and group 4, 76.9% (95% CI, 67.3%-86.5%).
evidence.note: WNT 100% survival, but group 3 is 73.7% and SHH lowest in this high-risk cohort.

evidence.quote: The WNT subgroup and non-metastatic Group 4 tumors with whole chromosome 11 loss or whole chromosome 17 gain were recognized as low-risk tumors that may qualify for reduced therapy.
evidence.note: WNT is low risk (favorable); no numeric WNT or Group 3 survival rates here.

claim: The most common cytogenetic mutation is isochromosome 17q, resulting from loss of the short arm (17p) with gain of genetic material from the long arm (17q).

evidence.quote: We have shown that an i(17q) is the most frequent abnormality in central nervous system primitive neuroectodermal tumors (PNETs; medulloblastoma), implicating the presence of a tumor suppressor gene which maps to 17p.
evidence.note: States i(17q) is the most frequent abnormality in medulloblastoma, linked to 17p loss. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Quote limited to CNS PNET/medulloblastoma; does not state most common overall or the 17p loss/17q gain.

evidence.quote: Group 4 is not well characterized, but harbors the most frequently observed chromosomal abnormality in MB, i17q, whose presence may confer a worse outcome.
evidence.note: Calls i17q the most frequently observed chromosomal abnormality in medulloblastoma. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Medulloblastoma not spelled out; 17p loss with 17q gain mechanism not stated.

claim: Time from symptom onset to diagnosis is usually short, typically 2-3 months.

evidence.quote: Eighty-eight patients were identified (63% male); median age was 6.9 years (interquartile range 4.8-9.2) and median symptom duration was 6 weeks (interquartile range 4-11).
evidence.note: Medulloblastoma median symptom duration 6 weeks, a bit under the claimed 2-3 months.

evidence.quote: The median prediagnostic symptomatic interval was 60 days (range, 0 to 3,480 days), with a median parental delay of 14 days (range, 0 to 1,835 days) and a median doctor's delay of 14 days (range, 0 to 3,480 days).
evidence.note: Median 60 days (about 2 months) across paediatric brain tumours, not medulloblastoma specifically.

claim: Osteosarcoma demonstrates a bimodal age distribution and most commonly occurs in the extremities.

evidence.quote: Osteosarcoma has a bimodal age distribution, having the first peak during adolescence and the second peak in older adulthood.
evidence.note: States bimodal age distribution with adolescent and older-adult peaks. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Occurrence in extremities not stated.

evidence.quote: Osteosarcoma commonly occurs in the long bones of the extremities near the metaphyseal growth plates.
evidence.note: States osteosarcoma most commonly arises in long bones of the extremities. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Bimodal age distribution not stated.

claim: Pain is often attributed to trauma or vigorous physical exercise, both of which are common in the patient population at risk.

evidence.quote: The patient may attribute symptoms to trauma or strenuous exercise, causing the patient to be managed conservatively.
evidence.note: Osteosarcoma patients may attribute symptoms to trauma or exercise; no frequency given and the at-risk-population point is absent.

claim: Symptoms are usually present for several months before the diagnosis is made, with an average duration of approximately 3 months.

evidence.quote: Average symptom duration was 5.4 ± 13.9 months (range, 0.1-84).
evidence.note: Pediatric bone sarcoma (osteosarcoma and Ewing) average symptom duration of 5.4 months. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Quote gives mean 5.4 months, not approximately 3 months.

evidence.quote: The preoperative duration of symptoms ranged from 2 weeks to 25 years (median, 6 months).
evidence.note: Median 6 months for extraskeletal osteosarcoma; a median, not an average, and a single subtype.

claim: The vast majority of patients (about 85 to 90%) with osteosarcoma undergo limb salvage, which involves removal of a tumor from a limb without removal of the entire limb itself.

evidence.quote: In addition, limb-sparing surgery has largely supplanted amputation, though the effect of this change on functional outcomes is controversial.
evidence.note: Limb-sparing surgery largely replaced amputation; no 85-90% proportion given.

claim: Variants in the TP53 gene are found in approximately 70% of patients with Li-Fraumeni syndrome (LFS), which is associated with increased risk of osteosarcoma, breast cancer, various brain cancers, soft tissue sarcomas, and other cancers.

evidence.quote: Most families fulfilling the classical diagnostic criteria harbour TP53 germline mutations.
evidence.note: Says most classic-criteria families carry TP53 mutations; no approximate 70% figure.

claim: About one-third of patients present with symptoms that arise either from the underlying tumor or from the presence of associated autoimmune paraneoplastic diseases.

evidence.quote: Patients with thymoma may experience symptoms associated with autoimmune paraneoplastic diseases (such as myasthenia gravis), which typically do not occur in patients with thymic carcinoma.
evidence.note: Paraneoplastic autoimmune symptoms occur in thymoma; no one-third proportion stated.

claim: The degree of invasion or tumor stage is generally thought to be a more important indicator of overall survival (OS).

evidence.quote: An asymptomatic history, surgical stage I disease, lymphocytic thymoma cell type, and complete resection favorably influenced prognosis.
evidence.note: Stage I is one of several favorable prognostic factors; stage not ranked above the others.

evidence.quote: Assessing the resectability of the tumor represents the first stage of the therapeutic strategy, as complete resection is the most significant prognostic factor on patient survival.
evidence.note: Names complete resection, not stage or invasion, as the most significant prognostic factor.

claim: The most accurate adverse prognostic marker is the invasiveness of the tumor.

evidence.quote: The results demonstrated that the factors affecting the prognosis may include resectability, postoperative irradiation or chemotherapy, MG, and tumor staging.
evidence.note: Tumor staging listed among several prognostic factors; invasiveness not singled out as most accurate.

evidence.quote: Despite the higher incidence of recurrences in type B3 and C thymoma the WHO classification did not prove to be a prognostic factor.
evidence.note: Histologic class was not prognostic here; does not name invasiveness as the strongest marker.

claim: Thymomas and thymic carcinomas are the most common mass of the anterior mediastinum.

evidence.quote: They are the most common anterior mediastinal tumors in adults.
evidence.note: Thymic epithelial tumors (thymoma and thymic carcinoma) are the most common anterior mediastinal tumors in adults. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Thymomas and thymic carcinomas not named ('They'); adults only.

evidence.quote: Benign or malignant tumors may originate from the thymus gland, with thymoma being the most common and accounting for 50% of anterior mediastinal tumors.
evidence.note: Thymoma alone accounts for 50% of anterior mediastinal tumors; thymic carcinoma not included.

claim: Late findings of the disease, typically occurring around 14 to 16 weeks of pregnancy, include signs and symptoms of thyrotoxicosis, including tachycardia and tremors, again caused by the high levels of circulating β-hCG.

evidence.quote: Trophoblastic tumors, hydatidiform mole, and choriocarcinoma often cause hyperthyroidism because they secrete very large amounts of hCG.
evidence.note: Hyperthyroidism in trophoblastic disease is caused by high hCG; no gestational age of 14-16 weeks or symptom list.

claim: Adrenocortical carcinomas (ACC) are very uncommon; these lesions are less common than cortical adenomas and pheochromocytoma.

evidence.quote: Adrenal adenomas were the most common tumors (31.9%), followed by pheochromocytomas (24.1%), and adrenal cortical carcinomas (11.2%); other lesions (e.g., cysts, myelolipoma, etc.) were rare.
evidence.note: In this surgical series carcinoma was less frequent than both adenoma and pheochromocytoma. Strict re-read: the quote does not state 'Very uncommon' not stated; only 11.2% share in one series.

evidence.quote: Adrenocortical adenoma was diagnosed in 73.1%; adrenocortical carcinoma in 7.7%; pheochromocytoma in 7.7% and less frequent adrenal lesions in 11.5%.
evidence.note: Carcinoma less common than adenoma, but equal to pheochromocytoma (7.7% each) in this incidentaloma series.

claim: ENSAT has shown that KI67 is the most powerful prognostic marker in both localized and advanced ACC and that higher Ki67 levels are consistently associated with worse prognosis.

evidence.quote: ENSAT stage and Ki67 predicted survival, type of surgery did not.
evidence.note: Ki67 predicted survival in this series; not stated as most powerful or split by localized versus advanced.

evidence.quote: (v) We suggest adjuvant mitotane treatment in patients after radical surgery that have a perceived high risk of recurrence (ENSAT stage III, or R1 resection, or Ki67 >10%).
evidence.note: Ki67 >10% used as a high-recurrence-risk marker; not described as the most powerful prognostic marker.

claim: The median overall survival (OS) of all ACC patients is about 3-4 years.

evidence.quote: Overall 5-year survival for all patients who underwent resection was 38.6% (median survival, 31.9 months).
evidence.note: Median survival 31.9 months (~2.7 years), resected patients only; below the claimed 3-4 years.

evidence.quote: In 8 systemic cases, the median overall survival from chemotherapy initiation was 7.2 months, and only 1 patient survived over 1 year.
evidence.note: Small mitotane series with much shorter median survival; subgroup, not all ACC patients.

claim: The worldwide incidence of ACC is 0.5 to 2 per 1 million people annually.

evidence.quote: Adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC) is a rare malignancy, with an estimated annual incidence of 0.7-2 cases per million and a median overall survival of 3-4 years.
evidence.note: Gives 0.7-2 per million annually, not 0.5-2; no explicit worldwide scope.

evidence.quote: With a reported incidence of 1 to 2 cases per million, adrenocortical cancer (ACC) is a rare disease with poor prognosis.
evidence.note: Gives 1 to 2 per million, a narrower range than 0.5 to 2; no annual or worldwide wording.

claim: Malignant peritoneal mesothelioma (MPM), on the other hand, is an aggressive tumor associated with asbestos exposure in 33% to 50% of cases.

evidence.quote: The material had come from a large number of sources, most of it having been traced by a history of occupational exposure to asbestos.
evidence.note: Says most peritoneal mesothelioma cases had asbestos exposure history, but gives no numeric proportion.
